label: The goods are under a mandatory Indian Standard
definition: The goods fall under a Quality Control Order, so they may not lawfully be manufactured, imported, sold or stocked without the Standard Mark. The specification clause must name the Indian Standard, the warranty must be a warranty of conformity to it, and the right to reject must survive.

authority.note: Compulsory use of the Standard Mark for goods notified under a Quality Control Order.
Sale by description — goods must correspond to the description.
Implied condition of fitness for purpose and merchantable quality.

b_lexicon.source_of_truth: BIS / DPIIT notified Quality Control Orders, published product-category list
b_lexicon.note: LIST NOT YET IMPORTED. This is the archetype of an imported enumeration: the government publishes the QCO list, so the concept is populated rather than invented. Detection is a lexicon match against the goods description, not an LLM judgement.

d_classifier.note: Used only to raise AMBIGUOUS when the description is too vague to match the lexicon — 'industrial components' — so the user is asked rather than the concept being silently dropped.

confirmation.question: Do these goods need a BIS Standard Mark (ISI mark) to be sold in India?
confirmation.why: If they do, selling them without it is an offence, and the agreement should require conformity to the specific Indian Standard rather than to a general description.

unresolved_behaviour.rationale: Neither direction is safe. Asserting a standard that does not apply writes a false obligation into the contract; denying one that does apply hides an offence. Where the lexicon does not match and the user cannot answer, the correct output is an OUTSIDE_KNOWN_SET disclosure naming the goods.

authoring_note: SUPPLY_GOODS_DESCRIPTION_001 already cites the BIS Act s.17 in its legal_basis, so the legal link is already recognised in the library — it simply is not conditional on anything.
